authority: A RECORD of what H4 decided and what it leaves owed. It is not answer authority: the cards are the product, batch_h4_manifest.json is the authorisation, and MIW_SOURCE_REGISTRY.json holds the sources.
scope: The five currentness/identity-sensitive roots held back from H3B-2 by instruction: CII improvement technologies, FAST, MACN latest outcome, the India health-declaration form, and the APEX manual.

root_dispositions.examiner_wording: Latest technologies to improve CII ratings
root_dispositions.why: The five CII cards explain the metric; QB7_I#q7/q8/q9 each carry ONE technology. The SET-level ask was uncovered. Re-verified against the live 759-card bank, where '\bCII\b' returns 92 hits over markup-stripped bodies and the nearest miss, QB1_F#q9, is an engine-room SFOC/WHR/hull card that mentions CII only in its CE-relevance paragraph.

root_dispositions.examiner_wording: Latest technologies - FAST valves, OCC, WAPS.
root_dispositions.why: Same examiner intent as AUG-0160 asked from the other side, and two of the three named technologies already had cards. One root answers both and carries FAST as a named maker example; a second card would have overlapped it entirely.
root_dispositions.identity: Wartsila Fuel Activated Sacless Technology - an INJECTOR upgrade, not a valve family. Verified at the maker's service catalogue, which also corrected two claims in MIW's own committed H4 evidence: the engine list includes RTA96C so it is not RT-flex only, and the page makes NO CII claim at all.

root_dispositions.why: 'apex' returns 6 hits on the live bank and every one is a false positive - CAPEX twice, Bloom's taxonomy twice, NOS-DCP as India's 'apex framework'. The pattern demonstrably finds the word, which is what makes the negative on the ISM sense credible. AUG-0194 is the 'why' limb of the same card, as its adjudication anticipated.

root_dispositions.examiner_wording: Name of Health declaration form used before arrival India
root_dispositions.why: The Maritime Declaration of Health, prescribed by the Indian Port Health Rules, 1955 - rule 5, form at Appendix 5 - read verbatim from the Ministry of Health's own portal. No card in the corpus names that instrument.
The identity card existed and carried no currency limb at all. The ask is a currentness cross-question, not a new root.

held_limbs.unknown: The commencement date of the Indian Ports Act, 2025 (s.1(2), by Gazette notification).
held_limbs.why_it_does_not_block: The answer to the examiner's question does not depend on it: s.85(2)(a) continues the 1955 Rules either way. The card gives assent 21 August 2025 and tells the candidate not to quote a commencement date.
held_limbs.evidence_needed: The commencement notification in the Gazette of India.
held_limbs.supporting: The 22 April 2026 draft rules G.S.R. 304(E) are framed as made 'on or after the date of coming into force of the Act', which is consistent with the Act not having commenced by then.

independent_review.shape: Clean-context, one per root group plus a structural/governance reviewer.
independent_review.producer_discipline: Every material finding was re-verified by the producer at primary source before any product change. Two reviewer claims were corrected in that process: the successor rule-set named in G.S.R. 304(E) is the Indian Port PUBLIC Health Rules, 2026; and the oralnotes file number is correct, not defective.
independent_review.most_valuable_finding: MS Notice 9 of 2014 was HELD LOCALLY the whole time, at meoclass1/oralnotes/assets/. I had grepped the oralnotes HTML, found nothing, gone to the network, been refused by two hosts, and recorded an access limit that did not exist. Reading the held scan produced three improvements no web source gave: the full 6.2.1.4 clause 'but not the other way round', s.6.2.1.5 on integrated systems, and s.8.1.1.5's own DOC-application requirement.
independent_review.second_most_valuable: The India card answered a 'before arrival' question without rule 4(1), the only genuinely pre-arrival duty in the instrument it cites - the 12-to-4-hours-out Standard Quarantine Message that supports radio pratique. Now the lead of the answer.

residues_for_h5.what: NO H-SERIES BATCH HAS A VALIDATOR, A MUTATOR OR A GATE. tools/oral/ holds validate_batch_{a..d,e1..e6,f1,f1b,g1..g4} and nothing for H1, H2, H3A, H3A-ORB, H3B-1, H3B-2 or H4. The seven H manifests' digest pins are asserted by nothing in the toolchain, and test_oral_release_infra.py's EXPECTED_BATCH_MANIFESTS names all seven plus batch_g4 as unexpected - it has been red since G4 shipped.
residues_for_h5.why_not_fixed_here: Building gates for H4 alone would leave H1-H3B ungated while implying the series is covered. This is release qualification, which the handover already places in H5.
residues_for_h5.scope: 8 manifests: batch_g4 plus the seven H-series.

residues_for_h5.what: held_limbs is read only by oral_manifest.py. validation.note: --keep-going was used deliberately. The default run stops at the first release-critical failure, and with two inherited reds at gates 5 and 6 that meant 61 gates never executed and H4 could not report coverage at all. Every failure was then classified by DERIVING the baseline in a clean worktree of bd7e076 - identity of failing check names, never counts.
